plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy. This is because I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid (as long as I win), so overbidding risks paying more than my value, and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to adjust for, I will bid exactly my value of $13 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. This maximizes expected profit because I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I only pay that second-highest bid, ensuring I never pay more than my value and always capture positive surplus when I win. I will bid my true value of $15.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. This holds because if I win, I pay someone else's bid, not my own—so shading my bid only risks losing profitable opportunities without reducing what I'd pay if I win. With a value of $47, I will bid exactly $47 to maximize expected profit.
